LA-2026-HB848.aiSummary: This law changes rules for all-terrain vehicle dealers and now includes golf carts in those rules. It says dealers must have repair and service facilities for these vehicles, or use a nearby third-party service provider, a manufacturer-backed service option, or a manufacturer-authorized service provider. Before a sale, dealers must give buyers written details about where warranty repairs will happen and may need to note if some service is done at a remote site.

LA-2026-HB75.aiSummary: This act creates a one-year pilot program for certain slot machine operators to offer more promotional play wagers, raising the untaxable amount from $5 million to $7 million. It also sets rules for how those proceeds are handled and says local governments and other local funds must not get less than they received in the 2025-2026 fiscal year. Licensees must file a report by March 1, 2027, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026, then ends June 30, 2027.

Summary of Senate Amendments to HB316

LA-2026-HB316.aiSummary: The bill would require teacher prep programs for early grades, special education, and secondary teachers to include training on how to teach reading and literacy, including how to use reading screeners and student data. It would also require the state education department to create an adolescent literacy program, approve reading tests, and offer literacy training and coaching support for schools. Public schools would have to review student reading and related support plans each year in the first eight weeks of school. The act takes effect on August 1, 2026.

It also updates who at therapeutic group homes must get a background check.

documents.label: Senate Green Sheet Digest for HB211
Summary of Senate Amendments to HB211

LA-2026-HB211.aiSummary: Creates a Homelessness Court program in district courts to give eligible people experiencing homelessness a treatment-based court process. It lets a judge place qualifying defendants on supervised treatment and probation for at least 12 months, with counseling, job and housing help, and court-ordered drug or alcohol testing. It also creates a new crime for unauthorized camping on public property and bars public camping and temporary outdoor living, with some exceptions and notice rules. The law took effect when it was signed and became Act No. 788.
